text_blocks.snippet: HIV-1 has four groups (M, N, O, and P), with Group M being the most prevalent and responsible for the global pandemic. Within Group M, there are nine recognized subtypes, often referred to as clades: A, B, C, D, F, G, H, J, and K. Subtype C is the most common globally, followed by subtypes A and B. These subtypes, along with circulating recombinant forms (CRFs), contribute to the diversity of HIV-1.
